messages.content:
logsift skips every line from our pay-batch hosts, because their older collector writes
the time as `14/Oct/2026:10:05:00` instead of ISO 8601 (see examples/pay-batch-2026-10-14.log).
That form has no time zone: it is the host's own clock, and data/host-offsets.json lists
the UTC offset of each pay-batch host. We also want to cut the noise when reading a log.
Please add:

- Support for the second timestamp format in logsift show and logsift summary. A line in
  that form is converted to UTC with the offset of the host that wrote it, so it prints
  and filters like any other entry and merges with ISO lines in time order. A new option
  --host-offsets FILE names the offsets file (same layout as data/host-offsets.json); a
  line from a host that the file does not list is skipped with a warning like any other
  line logsift cannot read.
- Without --host-offsets, logsift should use data/host-offsets.json, so that the
  pay-batch logs in examples/ show the right times when I run logsift from the repository.
- A --min-level LEVEL option on both commands that keeps only the entries at that level
  or more severe (so --min-level WARN keeps WARN, ERROR, and FATAL). The level name is
  accepted in any letter case; a name that is not a level should print an error and
  exit with status 2.

Logs in the ISO format, and everything else logsift does today, should work exactly as
before.

```json
{
  "thought": "I will add support for the second timestamp format in logsift and implement the --host-offsets and --min-level options.",
  "tool": "edit",
  "args": {
    "path": "logsift.py",
    "old": "def parse_timestamp(timestamp):",
    "new": "def parse_timestamp(timestamp):
    if ' ' in timestamp and '/' in timestamp:
        # Handle the new timestamp format
        date_parts = timestamp.split(' ')[0].split('/')
        time_parts = timestamp.split(' ')[1].split(':')
        year, month, day = int(date_parts[2]), int(date_parts[1]), int(date_parts[0])
        hour, minute, second = int(time_parts[0]), int(time_parts[1]), int(time_parts[2])
        host_offset = get_host_offset(timestamp.split(' ')[0])
        utc_time = datetime.datetime(year, month, day, hour, minute, second) + datetime.timedelta(hours=host_offset)
        return utc_time
    else:
        # Handle the existing timestamp format
        return datetime.datetime.strptime(timestamp, '%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S')"
  }
}
```
